issues.description: Behavior change smuggled into a 'just adding types' patch — pan/zoom now throw on empty domain
issues.detail: The PR description claims 'Everything else should have same runtime behavior as before, I just added types.' That is a lie the diff tells on itself. The new isNonEmpty guards call error() on empty domains, which previously returned [NaN, NaN] silently. That is a real behavior change that callers upstream in vega may rely on. THREE-PATCHES: split this into (1) types only, (2) the empty-domain runtime check with its own justification and changelog note, (3) anything else. As-is the commit message is wrong about what the commit does, and that wastes the next maintainer's time when they git-blame this.

issues.description: coerceNumber silently converts null/NaN to 0 — this is a real semantic change from toNumber
issues.detail: The old panLinear/zoomLinear passed toNumber directly as lift. toNumber returns null for unparseable input, which then propagated as NaN through arithmetic — visible garbage. The new coerceNumber does `toNumber(x) ?? 0`, turning bad input into a silent 0. That changes the output of panLinear([null, 10], 0.5) from [NaN, NaN] to something finite and wrong. The comment even brags about it: 'Unlike toNumber, coerceNumber always returns a number.' That is BAD-TASTE — papering over a type mismatch with a runtime lie to make the compiler happy. Fix the types, don't fix the values.

issues.description: Local identity rebinding instead of importing from accessors.js
issues.detail: The original imported `identity` from './accessors.js'. The new file drops that import and redefines `const identity: TransformFn = x => x;` locally. Either accessors.identity has the wrong type signature (in which case fix it there, where every other caller benefits) or this is a gratuitous local copy that will drift. Pick one. Don't fork the codebase's identity function inside one module because the types didn't line up.

issues.description: Domain type is misleading — declared as number[] but immediately narrowed to NonEmptyArray, and return type Domain=[number,number] hides what actually happens
issues.detail: The public signatures take `domain: number[]` and return `Domain` ([number, number]). If the function requires non-empty, the parameter type should be NonEmptyArray<number> and push the check to the caller boundary where it belongs — that is the whole point of typing this. As written, every caller still has to runtime-check, the type system gives them nothing, and the isNonEmpty guard is pure overhead. Either make the public type honest (NonEmptyArray) or drop the runtime throw. Don't do both halfway.

issues.description: peek overload ordering is fine but the second signature is redundant with the implementation signature
issues.detail: The two declared overloads plus the implementation signature work, but the second overload `peek<T>(array: readonly T[]): T | undefined` duplicates the implementation signature exactly. TypeScript allows it; it is still noise. One overload + the impl would be enough. Minor.

issues.description: Test coverage for the new throw is thin — only panLinear and zoomLinear, not panLog/panPow/panSymlog/zoomLog/zoomPow/zoomSymlog
issues.detail: If you are going to add a runtime check to seven functions (or eight), test seven functions. Two spot checks against the linear variants is the kind of coverage that ages into a regression when someone later refactors pan() or zoom() and the check moves. Loop over the exported functions or add the parametrized cases. Cheap.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The patch is sold as a pure typing refactor and then quietly changes runtime behavior in two ways: an empty-domain throw and a coerceNumber that turns null into 0 where toNumber used to propagate NaN. Either of those may be the right call, but they must not ride in on a commit message that says 'same runtime behavior as before' — that is exactly the kind of patch that bites a maintainer six years from now. THREE-PATCHES: split types from the empty-domain throw from the toNumber-to-0 swap, each with its own justification. Also: don't fork identity locally, and either make the public type NonEmptyArray<number> or drop the runtime guard — picking both is half-typing.
